observed.failing_step: App imports on a clean machine

notes: Mechanism: binary (C ABI) incompatibility. scikit-learn 1.2.2 ships cp311 wheels whose Cython extensions were compiled against NumPy 1.x, and its metadata says only 'numpy>=1.17.3' (the '<2.0' cap exists from 1.3.x on), so pip installs it next to the pinned numpy==2.4.4 without complaint. Package pair: scikit-learn 1.2.2 + numpy 2.4.4. 'Install dependencies' succeeds ('pip check' reports 'No broken requirements found'), then 'App imports on a clean machine' fails, the later 'Run smoke tests' step is skipped, and there is no pytest summary. sklearn is imported indirectly: api/services/chunking_service.py:24 imports langchain_text_splitters, whose __init__ imports sentence_transformers, whose util/similarity.py does 'from sklearn.metrics import pairwise_distances'; sklearn/utils/__init__.py then loads the compiled murmurhash module. Observed on python:3.11-slim (Python 3.11.17): the traceback ends with 'File "sklearn/utils/murmurhash.pyx", line 1, in init sklearn.utils.murmurhash' and "ValueError: numpy.dtype size changed, may indicate binary incompatibility. Expected 96 from C header, got 88 from PyObject". The traceback never names a version, and our code never imports sklearn directly; the agent has to connect the .pyx frame to the requirements.txt diff. The fix is restoring scikit-learn==1.8.0.
